general_notes_all_shape_codes: Values for minimum radius (r) and end dimension (A), per Table B.1, apply to all shape codes.

Dimensions in parentheses are free dimensions (absorb permissible deviation). If a different dimension must absorb tolerance than the one shown in parentheses for a standard shape, the shape must be redrawn and coded 99, with the actual free dimension shown in parentheses.

BS8666 Figures 4, 5, 6 should be used to interpret bending dimensions (external reference, not reproduced here).

Note 1: Length equations for shapes 14, 15, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 34, 35, 36, 46 are approximate; where bend angle > 45deg, length should be calculated more accurately (true centreline length vs specified overall dims differ); near 90deg bends, prefer shape code 99 with a fully dimensioned sketch.
Note 2: 5 or more bends may be impractical within permitted tolerances.
Note 3: For shapes with straight + curved lengths (12, 13, 22, 33, 47), largest practical mandrel size for a continuous curve is 400mm (see BS8666 Clause 10).

Note 4: Stock lengths available in a limited number of lengths (e.g. 6m, 12m). Dimension A for shape code 01 is indicative; actual delivery length by agreement with supplier; tolerances per relevant product standard (e.g. BS449:2005 cited, likely a scan/OCR error for a different standard number — flagged in gaps).

legacy_minimum_leg_length_rules_by_grade.description: Minimum bend-leg dimensions (A or B) for the legacy BS4466-era shapes, expressed by reinforcement GRADE rather than by the BS8666-era Table B.1's bar-SIZE-only P value. This is a materially different rule structure from Table B.1 and should be kept as a distinct, separately-applicable historical rule, not merged with Table B.1.
legacy_minimum_leg_length_rules_by_grade.engineering_meaning: Analogous in purpose to Table B.1's minimum end projection P (both exist to guarantee a bend has enough straight leg to develop bond/avoid splitting), but keyed to GRADE (460 vs 250) rather than to bar SIZE alone as Table B.1 is. A generator supporting historical (pre-BS8666) drawings must select this grade-based rule instead of Table B.1's size-based P for that era.

legacy_BS4466_shape_formulas_pre_BS8666.relationship_to_BS8666_catalogue: This legacy set is clearly the direct ancestor of the BS8666 shape-code catalogue captured elsewhere in this file: several formulas are structurally identical (e.g. 'A+B-0.5r-d' here vs BS8666 shape 11's 'A+B-0.5r-d'; '2(A+B)+12d' here vs BS8666 shape 51's minimized form '2A+2B+max(16d,160)'). A compiler generating period-accurate drawings pre-2000 should use THIS formula set (with the grade-based minimum-leg rule), and post-2000 should use the numbered BS8666 catalogue (with Table B.1).
